decisions.design: Agreed with the Guardian before building: the one-row primary key of the existing mute tables is kept; every later change is an event in a new table; one helper per store says whether a request is muted now and every reader asks it. Muted now is the newest event by its sequence number (never by a clock), or the first mute row when there is no event. A change from not muted to muted, by the page or by a mute link, always records an event; already muted by either route writes nothing.
decisions.authority: Only the person the request belongs to (the signed-in person who owns the request, same subject and issuer) can unmute or mute again. Workspace membership alone is not enough. Anyone else, and an unknown request, get the same refusal.
decisions.commands: One command id per decision. A repeat of the same decision returns the same answer and changes nothing; the same id for another decision or another request is refused; asking for the state a request already has records nothing and does not use the id up.
decisions.noBackSend: Unmute never queues, re-queues or sends. Messages suppressed while muted stay suppressed, a message made while muted is refused and leaves no row, and mail resumes only for messages made after the unmute. Muting again also suppresses mail that is waiting, as the link does.
decisions.closedControl: Turning emails back on needs the sending control to be open and answers reason closed otherwise; turning them off never does.
decisions.linkMute: The mute link in an old email still works with no sign-in and now also mutes again after an unmute (it writes an event). Its answers and refusals are unchanged.
decisions.audit: customer.mission_mail.muted/unmuted and customer.notification.muted/unmuted, ids only, in the same events and audit trail the first mute uses.
decisions.process: The two migration files were written before their database tests; the tests were then shown to fail with the migration file removed (8 of 8 in each store) and to pass with it. The muted requests spec was written after the component; a mutation that removes the dialog lock made its in-flight test fail.
decisions.moveTiming: Codex P2, verified: a Move is set in one transaction and enqueued in another up to ten minutes later, so a Move set before or during a muted period could send after an unmute. 0004 adds notification_muted_since(request, since) (muted at that moment, muted after it, or muted now) and enqueue_move_notifications asks it with the Move's creation time. Three tests: set before the mute, set while muted, both enqueued after the unmute queue nothing; a Move set after the unmute queues. The first two failed before the fix. 0004 is not installed anywhere, so it was edited in place. Mission mail has no such window: its enqueue runs in the request's own flow and a mute suppresses what is waiting.
decisions.labels: Codex P2, verified: customer.private_requests carries no title, so every muted request would have read 'A request you sent'. The page now labels each by 'Request sent <date and time>' from createdAt, the same wording the saved requests list falls back to. A test calls the real service and shows the response has no title.
decisions.guardianReview: Guardian findings (stamp auth-fa31a07b2d0e) folded into this push. (1) notification_muted_since returns true if any muted period overlaps the time from the Move's creation: muted at that moment (newest event at or before it by sequence number, else the first mute row if made by then), or a mute recorded at or after it, or muted now; tests: Move before the mute then mute and unmute before the enqueue, Move during a mute, Move after the unmute. (2) enqueue_move_notifications now checks after both advisory locks, the ones a mute takes (race test: a mute that commits while the enqueue waits for its lock is seen; it fails with the check before the lock), and notification_valid asks the since-check with the message's own creation time. (3) Mission mail only ever queues one request-received message per request, so an unmute there resumes nothing: the receipt-email rows have no button and say so in words; the database commands stay for any later kind. (4) Unmute is disabled with the reason while the reminder control is closed. (5) Both helpers order by event sequence, never by a clock; the one old row counts only when there is no event. (6) A replayed command answers with the current state, and the same command id on another request, or at the same moment from two requests, gets the same 42501 refusal (never a raw unique violation). (7) A mute link when already muted by either route returns already true and records nothing; any change to muted from the link also records an event, so the answer never depends on which route came first. (8) Revoked requests are left out of the lists and cannot be changed; the unmute record is strict (a missing executor fails the unmute), the mute record is not.
decisions.receiptRows: The receipt-email rows say 'Receipt email', not 'Receipt and progress emails': mission mail has no progress email, only the one request-received message.
